## Haliru Bello’s corruption case (EFCC) — what the records show

### 1) Who and what the case is about
- **Official:** **Haliru Mohammed Bello** (former **Minister of Defence, 2011–2012**; former/acting **PDP Board of Trustees** leadership).
- **Case theme:** Part of the wider **Dasuki “arms funds”** investigation—money released for national security/arms procurement was allegedly diverted for **2015 election-related political purposes**.
- **Status:** **Ongoing** (no final judgment yet). EFCC case records show **no conviction or acquittal** as of the latest updates (March 2024).

### 2) Core allegation and amount
- The prosecution case is built around an alleged **₦300 million** payment said to have come from the **Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA)** under **Col. Sambo Dasuki (rtd.)**.
- **Key transaction date:** **17 March 2015** — ₦300m allegedly transferred from the NSA/CBN-side source into a **Sterling Bank** account operated by **BAM Projects and Properties Ltd** (linked to Bello’s son).  
- Context in the records: the ₦300m is described as part of a broader **₦30 billion** released for “security issues” (arms/Boko Haram operations). Some profile summaries in the database display **₦30bn** as a wider-context figure, while Bello’s *specific* alleged receipt in this case is **₦300m**.

### 3) Defendants / co-accused in this case
From EFCC case files, the defendants were:
- **Haliru Mohammed Bello**
- **Abba Mohammed Bello** (his son) — **died January 2023** (so he is no longer a defendant as of the 2024 re-arraignment records)
- **BAM Projects and Properties Ltd** (company linked to Abba)

### 4) Charges filed (summary)
The EFCC filed a **4-count** case involving **money laundering** and **criminal breach of trust** themes, including allegations of:
- **Accepting proceeds of unlawful activity** (₦300m allegedly received knowing/ought-to-know it was proceeds of unlawful activity tied to Dasuki)
- **Conversion** of the ₦300m (described as purported “safe house” funds but allegedly used for **political campaign** purposes)
- **Retention/concealment** of the funds in the company’s bank account
- **Money laundering** under **Section 17(a)** of the Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act 2011 (as amended), punishable under **Section 17(b)**

All defendants **pleaded not guilty** at arraignment/re-arraignment (January 2016; March 2024).

### 5) Financial trail highlighted by EFCC forensic evidence
EFCC forensic testimony referenced in the case records describes rapid movements after receipt, including transfers to entities such as:
- **Kumugumu Ltd** (e.g., **₦137m**)
- **North Pole Ltd** (e.g., **₦178m**)
- **Hijra Textiles Ltd** (e.g., **₦163m**, stated to be on Bello’s instruction in the records)
- Cash withdrawals (recorded as **₦20m** in two tranches of ₦10m)
- Transfer to **Abba Bello’s personal savings** (e.g., **₦50m**)

*(The records note some figures may overlap as different “legs” of the same overall flow, but the consistent principal amount in this case is ₦300m.)*

### 6) Court history and key events
- **Charges filed:** **26 Dec 2015** (case timeline record)
- **Arraignment:** **7 Jan 2016** (Federal High Court, Abuja per records). Bello appeared **in a wheelchair** and was transferred to hospital when the matter was adjourned; his son was **remanded** pending bail hearing.
- **Feb 2016:** EFCC forensic witness (**Roukayya Ibrahim**) testified the ₦300m was **not** payment for any executed NSA contract; **Bashir Yuguda** (former Minister of State for Finance) is named in the records as a **facilitator** of the transaction.
- **Bail:** Bello was granted bail (Justice **Ahmed Mohammed**). EFCC later stated bail was **once revoked** for breach of conditions, but it was subsequently restored.
- **Reassignment / re-arraignment:** **18 Mar 2024**, before **Justice Peter Lifu**, after reassignment from Justice Ahmed Mohammed (elevated to Court of Appeal). Bello and **BAM Projects** were re-arraigned on an amended charge; plea: **not guilty**. Trial dates were set for **7–8 May 2024** (per case records).

### 7) Outcome so far
- **No final outcome yet**: as of the latest available case data (March 2024), it remains **ongoing** with **no conviction or acquittal** recorded.

If you want, I can also summarise **(a)** what evidence the EFCC says it relies on (witnesses/bank documents), or **(b)** how Bello’s case connects procedurally to the separate **Dasuki** prosecutions.

## James Onanefe Ibori (Former Governor, Delta State 1999–2007) — EFCC/UK case snapshot

### 1) Charges (Nigeria + UK)

**Nigeria (EFCC)**
- **Kaduna Federal High Court (arraignment: 12 Dec 2007):** **103 counts** including **money laundering** and **abuse of office** (EFCC lead counsel recorded as **Rotimi Jacobs**). Key allegations listed in the charge narratives include:  
  - **Alleged bribe to EFCC (26 Apr 2007):** **₦1.8 billion (~$15m)** cash allegedly offered to influence the investigation (Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act reference appears in the case file).  
  - **Afribank share purchases using allegedly concealed funds:** **₦280m** (Lipopo Nigeria Ltd) and **₦220m** (Kent) allegedly used to buy shares in fictitious names.  
  - **Delta State funds allegedly diverted:** **₦5bn** allegedly transferred from Delta State accounts to buy Afribank shares via a fictitious company.  
  - **Personal enrichment transfers:** entries include **₦5m** and **₦1m** moved from Delta State accounts to Ibori’s personal **GTB** account (as particularised in the charges summary).

- **Asaba Federal High Court (verdict: 17 Dec 2009):** EFCC filed **170 counts** of corruption/abuse of office after the matter was transferred; Ibori was **discharged and acquitted** at first instance (later overturned on appeal—see outcomes below).

**United Kingdom (Southwark Crown Court)**
- **Guilty plea (27 Feb 2012):** Ibori pleaded guilty to **10 counts** of:
  - **Money laundering**
  - **Conspiracy to defraud**
- UK case particulars in the records include:
  - **V‑Mobile transaction fraud:** **$37m** allegedly siphoned from sale of Delta State’s V‑Mobile stake; laundered via offshore structures and associates (including solicitor **Bhadresh Gohil** referenced in UK proceedings).
  - **“General plunder”/systematic theft** during 1999–2007 with laundering of proceeds through the UK.
  - **Fraudulent qualification to hold office:** alleged false details (DOB/criminal record concealment) used to become governor (raised in UK prosecution narrative).

---

### 2) How much was allegedly stolen (amounts cited in the case records)

Case records cite multiple figures (different authorities/contexts):

- **British police estimate (reported 2012):** **$250 million** stolen over eight years as governor.  
- **Amount admitted in UK court via plea:** **£50 million** (Ibori’s guilty plea basis).  
- **UK sentencing judge’s assessment:** total may be **“in excess of £200 million”** (judge’s statement on potential scale beyond the admitted sum).  
- **EFCC/Nigeria “second wave” allegation (2010 reopening):** **₦40 billion** (also described as about **$266m** in the file’s conversion).  
- **Database summary card total alleged:** shown as about **₦380bn** in one profile card and **₦399bn** in another (both tagged “summary [convicted]”, reflecting aggregation/normalisation in the profile layer).

**Asset restraint / recovery figures appearing in records**
- **UK asset freeze (Aug 2007):** about **£17m** (≈ **$35m**) frozen.  
- **UK confiscation order (21 Jul 2023):** **£101.5m** ordered confiscated.  
- **Returned to Nigeria (Mar 2021):** **£4.2m** returned under the UK–Nigeria asset return MoU (noted as ~2.7% of the targeted amount in the same records).

## Joshua Dariye — EFCC corruption case (Plateau State)

### 1) Who he is / context
- **Joshua Chibi Dariye** was **Governor of Plateau State (May 1999–May 2007)** and later **Senator for Plateau Central** (per case records).
- The case centred on **diversion/mismanagement of Plateau State ecological funds** and related **criminal breach of trust / misappropriation**.

### 2) Investigation background (UK angle)
- Case records note he was **arrested in London by the UK Metropolitan Police** on **20 Jan 2004** (some sources in the file also cite **Sept 2004**) during a **money laundering investigation**.
- A key prosecution witness was **UK Metropolitan Police detective Peter Clark**, who testified about the London investigation, cash movements, and that Dariye **jumped bail**.

### 3) Nigerian charges and core allegation
- **EFCC arraigned Dariye in July 2007** at the **FCT High Court, Gudu, Abuja** on **23 counts**.
- The allegations included diversion of ecological funds—case excerpts cite figures including **₦1.62 billion** (and some references in the records also cite about **₦1.126 billion**).
- One specific factual detail in the case file: funds meant for Plateau State were allegedly **paid into an account in the name of an unregistered company, “Ebenezer Retnan Ventures,” at All States Trust Bank Plc**, rather than a Plateau State Government account.

### 4) Court proceedings (why it took long)
- **Trial Judge:** **Justice Adebukola Banjoko** (FCT High Court).
- **Prosecution:** EFCC, led by **Rotimi Jacobs, SAN** (with **Tayo Olukotun**).
- **Defence:** **G. S. Pwul, SAN** (and **Festus Jombo** at appeal stage).
- Major delay driver: Dariye’s **jurisdiction challenge** (arguing he should be tried in Plateau, not FCT) was dismissed by the trial court (13 Dec 2007), but he pursued appeals up to the **Supreme Court**.  
  - The **Supreme Court (27 Feb 2015)** dismissed his appeal and ordered accelerated hearing/submission for trial.
- The prosecution called **10 witnesses** (including **Peter Clark**). Records note exhibits such as **bank documents, property records, and certified court orders**.
- **Amended charge** was accepted **9 May 2016**; prosecution closed its case around June 2016; conviction came in 2018.

### 5) Outcome (conviction, sentence, appeals)
- **Convicted:** **12 June 2018**
  - **Convicted on:** **15 of 23 counts**
  - **Counts dismissed:** **8** (noted as duplicity/insufficient evidence in the case file)
  - **Initial sentence:** **14 years’ imprisonment** (sentences ordered to run concurrently)
- **Court of Appeal (Abuja), 16 Nov 2018 (Justice Stephen Adah-led panel):**
  - **Conviction upheld**
  - **Sentence reduced to 10 years** (court said the trial court “went too far” with the maximum sentence; also referenced “first offender” considerations)
  - A diversion count sentence referenced in the records was reduced from **2 years to 1 year**, with sentences still running concurrently.
- **Supreme Court:** Case records state it **affirmed the 10-year sentence** (the exact date of that final affirmation isn’t specified in the collected excerpts).

### 6) Imprisonment, pardon, release
- **Custody:** **Kuje Correctional Centre, FCT**
- Served from **June 2018** until release in **August 2022** (records describe this as ~4 years).
- **Presidential pardon:** **14 April 2022**
- **Release:** **8 August 2022**

### 7) Key names that feature prominently in the case records
- **Justice Adebukola Banjoko** (trial judge)
- **Justice Stephen Adah** (Court of Appeal)
- **Rotimi Jacobs, SAN** (EFCC lead prosecutor)
- **Peter Clark** (UK Met Police witness)
- **Kawu Mohammed** (EFCC Asset Forfeiture/Recovery; records mention property/rent recovery evidence, including **₦67 million rent** linked to an Abuja property)
